capture_identities.label: after-runtime-profile
command:
import runpy,subprocess,sys
try:
 script=sys.argv.pop(1)
 runpy.run_path(script,run_name="__main__")
except subprocess.CalledProcessError as error:
 print("RECORDER STDOUT:",error.stdout,file=sys.stderr)
 print("RECORDER STDERR:",error.stderr,file=sys.stderr)
 raise

source_provenance_limit: Records without source_freeze_sha256 prove only their then-current unchanged marker and explicit parent-reviewed selection, not the final freeze identity. VM/JIT host/x86 unit records must carry the exact final production freeze digest; previous VM3/JIT4 are historical evidence only. No failed historical command was replaced automatically. Source-current identities are checked independently here.
fixture_repair: Compiler fixtures retain exact loaded-callee/source/message/pc+1 CFG assertions; their passing compiler run is selected separately from the failed bundled run. The NewError publication fixture uses outer.for_function for the actual physical frame context while retaining the distinct inline source pool. Runtime receiver ownership is retained by the cold forwarding branch after observe(1); compiler-hoisted CollectArguments is absent, and the measured Call0<New<Call1 region remains Array-only. Repairs are cfg test setup, not production semantic substitutes.
